records.label: cyber
records.why: On the July 2021 Pegasus scandal—dozens of governments (Mexico, India, Morocco, Hungary) using NSO Group's spyware to turn smartphones into spying tools (50,000+ numbers targeted per Amnesty/Forbidden Stories: activists, politicians, journalists), even Telegram's Pavel Durov spied on—arguing no system is safe (attackers need just one flaw), then pivoting to December's Log4j internet vulnerability (state spyware/vulnerabilities).

records.label: not_cyber
records.why: A 'how do I steal a Facebook account via phone' piece—framed as awareness but walking through methods of hacking a Facebook account via the phone and spyware; a low-skill account-hacking clickbait/SEO piece, not substantive cybersecurity subject matter.

records.label: cyber
records.why: An article on five ways WhatsApp can be hacked—leading with the October 2019 GIF remote-code-execution vulnerability (found by researcher Awakened) where a malicious GIF sent to a user could let the sender read the whole chat history and access files/photos/videos—affecting WhatsApp 2.19.230 on Android 8.1/9, responsibly disclosed and fixed by Facebook in 2.19.244 (vulnerability/hacking methods).

records.label: cyber
records.why: On the 2016 Bitfinex hack—Heather Morgan and Ilya Lichtenstein monitoring the crypto exchange's servers for weeks, studying its security controls, then finding a flaw to get the passwords to move funds; at 10:26am on Aug 2, 2016 they raised the daily withdrawal limit and, over 3h51m, stole 119,754 bitcoin (over half the exchange's holdings) to blockchain accounts they controlled (crypto exchange hack).

records.label: borderline
records.why: An article on Android firewall apps—noting Android security differs from PCs (you don't need a firewall as much, but many apps connect to the internet in the background without prior permission, one being malicious), so firewall apps give more control over which apps reach the internet (block IPs, control bandwidth)—recommending NetGuard (which runs as a local VPN); an Android firewall-app roundup/how-to (a weak signal).

records.label: cyber
records.why: A guide on treating ransomware on an infected device—explaining ransomware (malicious software cybercriminals use to encrypt all files and demand payment, with no guarantee of recovery even if paid)—and, when the black-and-red 'YOUR COMPUTER HAS BEEN LOCKED' message appears, steps to try (restoring from backup, booting via F8 to safe mode); a ransomware removal/treatment guide (ransomware).

records.label: cyber
records.why: An investigative piece on communications interception in Lebanon—WikiLeaks leaks revealing efforts by General Security, army intelligence, and two private firms to acquire 'total surveillance' spyware (spending millions to record every cellular/digital move)—asking whether Lebanese security agencies can hack citizens' phones and privacy, with sources admitting they contacted Hacking Team (state surveillance/spyware).

records.label: cyber
records.why: On Kaspersky researchers uncovering attacks exploiting a previously-unknown zero-day vulnerability in the Telegram desktop app—delivering multi-purpose malware (a backdoor or cryptominer)—via the Unicode RLO (right-to-left override, used for Arabic/RTL text) to disguise the file name of a malicious file (e.g. as an image), actively exploited since March 2017 for mining Monero/Zcash, with the attackers likely Russian (zero-day/malware).

records.label: not_cyber
records.why: An article on the reasons your site's Google ranking dropped—Google penalties for violating its policies (e.g. keyword stuffing) and other common SEO issues to fix—amid frequent Google updates; an SEO-troubleshooting piece, the 'malware'/'malicious files'/'spam' keywords are peripheral, not cybersecurity subject matter.

records.label: cyber

records.label: cyber

records.label: cyber

Paul Nakasone, also NSA director)—signaling cyber-warfare's growing importance as the US faces advanced hacking from Russia, China, and others—with military units trained to repel and launch cyberattacks, operating against groups like ISIS (state cyber command).

records.label: cyber

records.label: cyber
records.why: On researchers (Proofpoint) discovering the 'Smominru' (aka Ismo) malware that mines Monero—infecting 526,000+ computers worldwide using the NSA-developed 'EternalBlue' exploit (leaked by the Shadow Brokers, also behind 2017's WannaCry)—active since May 2017, mining ~24 Monero/day (~8,900 coins so far, ~$2.1M) (cryptomining malware).

records.label: not_cyber

records.label: cyber

records.label: cyber
records.why: A technical explainer on how anti-malware software identifies malware (viruses/spyware, etc.)—the key being the 'malware signature': how anti-malware reads a file's binary code and defines a signature as a distinctive sequence of bits unlikely to appear in the same order in any other program, used to fingerprint each malicious program; a malware-detection/signature explainer (infosec).

records.label: cyber
records.why: On the Israeli cyber-spy firm 'Quadream' shutting down after Israel's defense ministry refused it a license to sell its 'Reign' spyware to Morocco—Reign (a top competitor to NSO's Pegasus, with a Saudi client) able to infiltrate iPhones/Androids with 'zero clicks' (no victim action) to access all contacts, chats, and encrypted-app messages like WhatsApp (state spyware).

records.label: borderline
